_status: Design-authority transcription, not portfolio content. A1/A2 row LABELS and TARGETS come from STEP-01-CHARTER §3/§4 and STEP-02-HANDOFF §3 (3d). A3 comes from HANDOFF §5, which is the complete list — nothing else ships (C-12).
_measured_values: This file carries NO measured values and NO pass/fail statuses. Those are written by CI into data/generated/audit.json and rendered from there (C-30, C-35). When that file is absent — as on any first deploy — the measured column reads '— AT DEPLOY'. Hand-entering a score here would be the exact thing C-35 forbids.

Body text contrast vs page background

a2_charter_checks.check: Motion uses transform / opacity only; micro 150–250ms; transitions ≤ 400ms
Native scrolling only; slider is CSS scroll-snap with visible position
No preloaders, sound, trackers, cookies, third-party logos or assets
No contact-capable email or phone anywhere; contact via LinkedIn only
Interaction QA — no hover layer blocks or overlaps another interactive element
a2_charter_checks.basis_note: A person looked. One slice of this is automated (test_evidence_layer_never_covers_the_links_column), but the claim across every page and state was established by observation, so it is published as an observation with its date rather than as a machine verdict.

a2_charter_checks.check: All displayed values real; unverified items marked with an honest cross

a2_charter_checks.basis_note: The mechanical half is gated: tools/check_animations.py refuses the build (REASON=MOTION_NOT_REDUCED) if any timed transition cannot be switched off under prefers-reduced-motion. Whether the page remains COHERENT with motion off is a human judgement, observed and dated, so this row publishes the observation rather than a machine verdict for the whole claim.

a2_charter_checks.check: Every figure carries a version anchor and an evidence link

a4_limitations.limitation: No clickjacking control is possible: neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors, and no HSTS preload
a4_limitations.reason: GitHub Pages serves no custom HTTP response headers (charter §7), so X-Frame-Options and HSTS cannot be set. CSP is applied via meta instead — but CSP Level 3 §3.3 states that report-uri, frame-ancestors and sandbox are IGNORED when delivered by meta, so frame-ancestors is unavailable too. Verified against the specification 2026-08-06, not assumed. This is a WIDER gap than this row originally described: the modern replacement is as unavailable as the legacy header. frame-ancestors is deliberately omitted from the policy rather than written and ignored, because a directive that looks like protection and provides none is worse than a declared absence. There is also no report-only mode via meta, so the policy is enforced from the first deploy.
Only entries carrying real credential verification are accepted (C-27). The empty state is the designed state, not a missing feature. Obligation O-2.

a4_limitations.limitation: The visit counter shows a dash, not a count
a4_limitations.reason: v1.0.0 ships with zero third-party resources by decision: the counter's script publishes no stable SRI hash, so C-19 could not fully cover it. Decision D-03.

a4_limitations.limitation: C-05 (image formats, sizing, lazy-loading) reports MET-not-applicable
a4_limitations.reason: The committed design is pure typography; no content images ship, so the condition is satisfied because nothing it governs exists — which is not the same as passing a test. The generated Open Graph image is out-of-scope metadata and is never rendered in-page.

a4_limitations.limitation: Displayed project figures are resume-stated baselines, not live counts
a4_limitations.reason: The GitHub API returns no test count. Each figure carries the release tag or commit SHA it was stated against, plus a link to its source. The anchor fixes the version; it does not re-count. Decision D-02. Exception: the TS-Sentry entry is owner-measured and badge-corroborated, a stronger basis, stated as such in projects.json.

a4_limitations.limitation: One historical commit in this repo contains a contact-capable address
a4_limitations.reason: Defect D-21: the defect log briefly reproduced the address that defect D-01 was about. The working tree is clean and every commit is authored by a noreply identity, but commit e967e22 retains the string. Owner's decision, 2026-08-06: published history is not rewritten — a force-push would invalidate the hand-verified P3.1 close and would not achieve removal, since force-pushed commits remain fetchable by SHA. Declared here rather than hidden. The ledger records; it does not rewrite.

a4_limitations.limitation: Screen-reader verification covers the Home page only; Projects, Experience, Certifications and Audit are unverified by screen reader
a4_limitations.reason: C-08 is MET IN PART, declared under charter §8. An NVDA pass against a five-point checklist — title and heading walk, meaningful link names, marks silent, nav announces current page, clock silent over a one-minute listen — was performed on Home and passed all five. The other four pages were not examined. They share the same nav, footer, mark macros and heading structure, so there is a reasonable expectation they behave alike, but an expectation is not an observation and this site does not publish one as the other. The remaining pages are re-offered at every release under the same checklist; the limit narrows only when a page is actually examined. Note also that zero axe violations is not the same as accessible: automated tooling catches a minority of real barriers, which is why the screen-reader pass exists as a separate condition at all.

Charter §5 makes light mode optional and later, never at the cost of C-09. Deferred to v1.1 by owner decision (R-11); v1 ships dark-first by committed design. No charter amendment required — the charter already permits this.

_a4_resolved_note: Limitations that CLOSED. Kept and published rather than deleted: a register showing only what is currently broken teaches nothing about how the posture got here, and silently dropping a declaration is indistinguishable from never having made it. A limit leaves the active list only when it genuinely narrowed, with what closed it recorded.

a4_resolved.limitation: TS-Sentry test, defect and version metrics were unverified
a4_resolved.closed_by: Owner supplied measured figures — 1,230 tests at v1.0.0, 93.16% coverage against a 90% CI floor, mypy --strict clean across 164 files — from a local run corroborated by the repo's pinned CI and coverage badges. Obligation O-1 discharged; the card now renders a verification mark rather than an honest cross.

a3_animations.animation: Home — flagship row evidence reveal (pointer-events:none layer)
Projects — case slider, native CSS scroll-snap with visible scrollbar
All pages — link and nav hover state (instant colour swap, no transition)
Experience — receipts row reading state on hover and focus-within (background tint, body → bright text, instant)
a3_animations.note: Owner-directed addition to the handoff §5 list, 2026-08-06. Declared WHERE AM I, not WHAT CAN I DO: the rows carry no control, and claiming an affordance that does not exist is what C-12 exists to catch. Keyboard parity is :focus-within, never tabindex — dead tab stops would cost more against C-07 and C-08 than they gain. HONEST LIMIT: no receipts row currently contains a focusable element, so the focus half is inert until one does.

a3_animations.animation: All pages — cross-document view transition, vertical ledger-turn (header and footer persist; main turns out and in)
a3_animations.note: Added by the v1.1 motion amendment (MOTION_SPEC_v1_1.md, M-1), owner ruling 2026-08-10. Native CSS cross-document View Transitions: zero JS and zero library bytes (C-19). Duration is driven by --motion-vt so the single C-10 lever reaches it; the spec's prose governs over its illustrative code block, which showed a 250ms literal (reading R-13). Browsers without @view-transition ignore the at-rule and navigate normally — content is never hidden behind an API the browser lacks.

a3_animations.animation: Experience — register rows and receipt rules surface on scroll, scrubbed to scroll position (/experience/ only)
a3_animations.note: Added by the v1.1 motion amendment (MOTION_SPEC_v1_1.md, M-2), owner ruling 2026-08-10. CSS animation-timeline: view() — no JS and no scroll listeners (C-19, C-14). Duration is SCRUBBED, not timed: progress is bound to scroll position, so C-15's time caps do not bind and no millisecond value is invented for it. Wrapped in @supports so non-supporting browsers see every row and rule statically from first paint. Earns WHERE AM I because the reveal frontier is the reader's own position in the six-role register.

_a3_list_governance: Handoff §5 called this list complete at three. It is now four. 'Nothing else ships' is preserved as: THE LIST CHANGES ONLY BY RECORDED RULING, NEVER SILENTLY. tools/check_animations.py compares what actually ships against this declared list in both directions — shipping an undeclared animation fails the build, and declaring one that does not ship fails too.
